transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (NimbusWorks SRE Lead), Marcus Lee (NimbusWorks ML Engineer), Olivia Grant (NimbusWorks PM)

[00:00] Avery: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Avery from Redwood Inference, I'll hand it over to Samir to kick off the technical goals but quick intro, this is a POC scoping session focused on capacity sizing and autoscaling for your workload, specifically reserved GPUs plus burst strategy and fallback policies.
[00:18] Samir: Hey all, yeah thanks. Quick agenda, clarify success criteria, look at workload numbers, propose reserved GPU baseline, burst mechanics, fallback and compatibility, then benchmarks and timeline, sound good?
[00:32] Priya: Yep sounds good. We're mainly trying to prove we can meet p95 latency and cost targets under our peak without over-committing budget.
[00:40] Olivia: Also product wants a clear risk matrix - like what happens when reserved pool is saturated.
[00:46] Marcus: From infra side we care about autoscaler behavior, cold starts, GPU warm-ups, and KV cache effects.
[00:55] Samir: Great, can you share current traffic shape?
[01:00] Priya: Sure at a high level our steady is around 30 QPS for the LLM feature, peaks up to ~120 QPS during batch events, average response size variant 200-800 tokens. p95 target is 300ms for 256 token responses, p99 is softer at 800ms. These are customer-facing SLAs.
[01:25] Avery: Good. For the POC we'll need a sample prompt set and QPS histogram, and ideally a few representative long-tail prompts. Marcus, can your team export that?
[01:34] Marcus: Yes we can. I'll get two weeks of logs and a sample of 1k requests.
[01:38] Samir: For sizing: given 30 QPS steady and 120 QPS peak, recommended baseline is reserved capacity to handle steady plus buffer. Our initial proposal is a reserved pool that covers 40 QPS sustained and burst pool to cover peaks to 120 QPS.
[01:54] Priya: How does that translate to GPUs? We run mixed models, primarily a 13B-style open model quantized to 4-bit for cost.
[02:02] Samir: With 13B quantized, typical throughput per A100-80GB is around 12-20 QPS depending on batch config and request length. For your mixture I'd propose starting with 3 x A100 equivalents reserved (covers roughly 36-60 QPS depending on batching) and a burst pool of 3 additional instances to reach ~120 QPS. That gives a 6-GPU aggregate, 3 reserved + 3 burst.
[02:30] Olivia: Is burst immediate? Do we see cold start latency?
[02:34] Samir: Burst is usually fast if capacity is warmed or using pre-warmed burst instances. If we rely on cloud preemptible or on-demand spin-up, cold starts can be 30s-2min. We recommend pre-warmed burst nodes for production-like POC, or a tiered approach: warm instances for fast burst, and auto-add more if still needed.
[02:50] Priya: What's the cost difference? Pre-warming means paying for more reserved like compute, right?
[02:55] Avery: We offer a few pricing patterns in POC: reserved baseline at a discounted rate, burst at a higher rate while pre-warmed, and ephemeral burst (cheaper but longer cold starts). We'll include numbers in the POC pricing sheet.
[03:10] Marcus: We also want a fallback plan in case capacity is exhausted in a region.
[03:14] Samir: Two main fallback strategies: 1) fallback to a quantized/ distilled smaller model with compatible API to keep latency low at some quality cost; 2) fallback to a hosted lower-cost Redwood variant in another region or tier while preserving requests. You can also route non-critical traffic to a cached response or queue with priority.
[03:32] Priya: For the POC can we simulate fallback and measure quality degradation?
[03:36] Samir: Absolutely, part of the benchmark plan is to include a failover run: saturate reserved pool and observe how the system routes to burst and then to fallback models. We'll run quality evals on the sample prompts to quantify regression.
[03:50] Avery: Success criteria we heard: hit p95 latency <=300ms for 256 tokens on steady and p95 <=500-600ms on peak using the combined reserved+burst config; cost per 1M tokens within your target; no significant quality regression (delta <5% on your eval metric). Agree?
[04:08] Olivia: That aligns, product would accept up to 7% quality drop if latency is kept tight, but prefer <5%.
[04:16] Marcus: From ops, we need transparent logs for autoscaler decisions, per-request routing traces, and audit logs for compliance.
[04:24] Samir: We expose per-route dashboards, request-level traces, and audit logs; we can also push those to your SIEM. For POC we can keep 30-day retention.
[04:34] Priya: KMS and SSO are required for Private deployments; for POC we can use managed keys but need to evaluate encryption at rest.
[04:43] Avery: We'll include KMS integration notes. For a VPC/private POC we can arrange a private control plane with customer-managed networking, or run in Redwood Dedicated with encrypted volumes.
[04:56] Marcus: Back to sizing: can you explain batching and KV cache impact?
[04:59] Samir: Sure. Continuous batching increases throughput but can add a tail latency if you wait to fill a batch. We tune batching windows and max batch size per workload. KV cache (prefix cache) improves latency for repeated contexts by avoiding recomputation; for chat-like workloads with reuse it's huge. For your workload with many short distinct prompts, batching helps more than KV cache.
[05:22] Priya: Any guidance on autoscaler thresholds?
[05:25] Samir: Common pattern: scale up when avg CPU/GPU utilization >70% for 30s and scale down when <40% for 120s. For GPU-based inference we also look at request queue length and tail latency signals. We'll provide tuned defaults and you can adapt.
[05:42] Olivia: For the POC benchmark, what's the test plan?
[05:46] Samir: Plan: 1) baseline single-model run on reserved pool for steady traffic; 2) stress test to simulate peaks and observe burst scale-up; 3) failure test to exhaust burst and validate fallback; 4) quality/eval runs comparing outputs across fallback models. Each run includes telemetry capture (latency histograms, token cost, model outputs).
[06:02] Priya: How long will each run take? We need to schedule maintenance windows.
[06:06] Samir: Each run is typically 1-3 hours: baseline 1hr, stress 2hr with ramping, fallback test 1hr, plus analysis time. We'll coordinate a 2-3 day window to run everything.
[06:17] Marcus: Timeline for POC overall?
[06:19] Avery: Proposed: week 0 (this week) scoping and contract, week 1 setup (networking, test data, reserved pool), week 2 run benchmarks, week 3 analyze and deliver report and recommendation. So roughly a 3-week POC.
[06:33] Olivia: Sounds good. What metrics do you propose we use for quality/regression?
[06:36] Samir: Use a combination of automatic metrics (BLEU/ROUGE not great for chat; we recommend BERTScore/embedding similarity) and a small human eval panel for critical prompts. We'll report delta percentages and give examples of failures.
[06:48] Priya: On the reserved GPU numbers - if we start with 3 reserved + 3 burst, how easy is it to change mid-POC?
[06:55] Samir: We can adjust within hours for most clouds; for private on-prem it may take longer. For dedicated cloud pools we can increase burst capacity as needed. We'll monitor and suggest changes after baseline runs.
[07:08] Marcus: Any pitfalls to watch for?
[07:10] Samir: Main gotchas: under-estimating tail latencies from batching, cold KV caches after redeploy, noisy neighbors if using shared burst nodes, and warm-up time for large models. Also be explicit about model quantization differences between reserved and fallback variants.
[07:26] Priya: On audit/compliance, we need to preview SOC2 docs.
[07:29] Avery: We'll send SOC2 summary and security pack as part of the POC packet.
[07:33] Olivia: OK, can we capture the success criteria in writing?
[07:36] Avery: Sure — I'll summarize: 1) p95 latency <=300ms for 256 tokens on steady with reserved pool; 2) p95 latency <=500-600ms during peak with reserved+burst; 3) quality regression <5% vs baseline; 4) cost target X per 1M tokens (we'll fill exact figure after you share QPS histogram). We'll put these in the POC charter.
[07:55] Marcus: That works. Also, we want to see per-route cost breakdown in the dashboard during the POC.
[07:59] Samir: We'll enable token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards for the trial.
[08:05] Priya: Ok next steps recap?
[08:07] Avery: Action items: Priya provide QPS and targets; Marcus provide prompt set; Samir prepare benchmark harness and sizing proposal; Avery send POC pricing and security docs. We'll aim to start benchmarking week of 2025-02-18.
[08:22] Olivia: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the proposal and the run.
[08:26] Avery: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites. Bye.

Notes: transcript has occasional transcription errors and shorthand. References to product names: Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Console, KV cache, KMS, VPC. Benchmarks to include latency histograms, QPS ramping, failover/fallback routing trace, and human eval of regression.
